title: FBI National Crime Information Center apparently breached, CNN and NBC report
date_note: Date of the CNN report as relayed by Arab News (published 21 November, says CNN reported on Friday); the date of the intrusion is not stated.
place: Washington, DC, United States (FBI headquarters; location of the system not stated)
summary: CNN, relayed by Arab News, and NBC News reported an apparent breach of the FBI National Crime Information Center. AP, citing a person familiar, says the FBI is investigating; ABC says a law enforcement source confirmed the hack. On 24 November Director Kash Patel said "the matter is ongoing", CyberScoop reports.
plain: News outlets report a hack of the FBI's national criminal database; a law enforcement source told ABC News it was hacked. FBI Director Patel said on 24 November the matter is ongoing; who did it and the scale are unclear.
exec: A reported hack of a core US law-enforcement database; the FBI has given no details beyond saying the matter is ongoing, and the scale is unclear.

sources.name: NBC News (Ryan J. Reilly, Colleen Long, Kyla Guilfoil)
ABC News (Nicholas Kerr, Luke Barr), via ABC7 New York

validation.note: CNN (relayed by Arab News and CNN Brasil), NBC News, AP (via KSL) and ABC News (via ABC7) each cite their own anonymous sources; ABC says a law enforcement source confirmed the hack. The FBI declined to comment to AP and did not respond to ABC; no FBI or DOJ statement read, so status stays developing. Trump's quoted words (AP, ABC) are "it's not good"; EFE (ABC Color) calls his remarks a confirmation. CNN original answered 451. CyberScoop (24 Nov): Patel declined details at a DOJ press conference, citing an ongoing investigation; status kept developing.

review.note: stale wording: plain and exec said the FBI has not commented; Patel said on 24 Nov the matter is ongoing (CyberScoop); reworded
